summary.text: Tom Tiffany is the U.S. Representative for Wisconsin's 7th District and the Republican nominee for governor with running mate David Varnam, a former mayor of Lancaster.

A dairy-farm native who worked in petroleum distribution and ran an excursion boat business before entering politics, he served in the Wisconsin Assembly and Senate and won a May 2020 special election to Congress.

paragraphs.text: Tom Tiffany was born in Wabasha, Minnesota, and grew up on a dairy farm near Elmwood, Wisconsin.
He graduated from Elmwood High School in 1976 and earned a B.S. in agricultural economics from the University of Wisconsin-River Falls in 1980.
He managed the petroleum division of High Plains Cooperative in Plainview, Minnesota, before moving to Minocqua, Wisconsin, in 1988 to manage petroleum distribution for Zenker Oil Company.

With his wife, Chris, he operated an excursion business, Wilderness Queen Cruise Line, on the Willow Flowage from 1991 to 2006, moved it to Rhinelander in 2007 and sold it in 2012, and he served as supervisor of the town of Little Rice from 2009 to 2013.
Tiffany lost state Senate races in 2004 and 2008, then won election to the Wisconsin Assembly in 2010 and the state Senate in 2012.
In the Senate he was a member of the Joint Finance Committee and chaired the Committee on Sporting Heritage, Mining and Forestry.

After U.S. Rep. Sean Duffy resigned in September 2019, Tiffany won the February 18, 2020 Republican primary and defeated Tricia Zunker in the May 12, 2020 special election, and he was sworn in on May 19, 2020.
In Congress he serves on the Judiciary and Natural Resources committees and is a member of the Freedom Caucus.
He announced his campaign for governor on September 23, 2025.
Tiffany and his wife, Christine, have three children.
